sentences.en: Today, we are going to be talking about emotional eating.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将讨论情绪性进食。

sentences.en: Our relationship with food is so much more psychological than we think it is,
sentences.zh: 我们与食物的关系比我们想象的要心理化得多，

sentences.en: so much more emotional, so much more intricate and nuanced than just hunger and fullness and nutrients and energy.
sentences.zh: 要情绪化得多，要复杂和微妙得多，绝不仅仅是饥饿与饱腹、营养与能量的关系。

sentences.en: Food can be used to self-medicate, to manage our emotions.
sentences.zh: 食物可以被用来进行自我治疗，用来管理我们的情绪。

sentences.en: It has a biological impact on our mental state.
sentences.zh: 它对我们的精神状态有着生理上的影响。

sentences.en: And I think with a rise in things like diet culture, it's also become really equated with ideas of self-worth and self-esteem,
sentences.zh: 我认为随着诸如减肥文化等现象的兴起，食物也开始与自我价值和自尊的概念紧密挂钩，

sentences.en: such that it's no longer just the thing that we use to fuel ourselves.
sentences.zh: 以至于它不再仅仅是我们用来补充能量的物质。

sentences.en: It has a much more complicated relationship with how we see ourselves and how we process our emotions.
sentences.zh: 它在我们如何看待自己以及如何处理情绪方面，有着更加复杂的关系。

sentences.en: I want to be really candid here.
sentences.zh: 我想在这里坦诚相告。

sentences.en: I don't think that I personally have ever had a perfect relationship with food.
sentences.zh: 我认为我个人从未与食物建立过完美的健康关系。

sentences.en: I think right now, where I'm at, is probably the closest I've ever gotten.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在的状态，可能是我有史以来最接近完美的一次。

sentences.en: And I haven't spoken it much about on the podcast before because it is really vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 我以前在播客里没怎么谈过这个，因为这真的非常戳中我的软肋。

sentences.en: But, you know, I grew up in the time of Thinsbo and Tumblr.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我是伴随着“骨感美（Thinsbo）”和汤博乐（Tumblr）的时代长大的。

sentences.en: And for a long time, food really controlled my life in an unhealthy way, whereby I was either highly restrictive, especially in my teen years,
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，食物以一种不健康的方式控制了我的生活，导致我在青少年时期要么极度克制，

sentences.en: constantly needing to eat the right way, being worried about calories, or on the flip side, I felt completely beholden to food and to my cravings.
sentences.zh: 时刻需要用正确的方式进食、担心卡路里，要么在另一方面，我感觉自己完全沦为了食物和食欲的奴隶。

sentences.en: I never really experienced hunger.
sentences.zh: 我从未真正体验过什么是真正的饥饿。

sentences.en: I used food as a coping mechanism to elevate my mood or counter my stress or feel emotionally fulfilled when I was lonely or felt rejected.
sentences.zh: 我把食物当作一种应对机制来提升情绪、对抗压力，或者在感到孤独和被拒绝时寻求情感上的满足。

sentences.en: Part of that journey was to do with emotional eating, responding to what I was feeling through consumption rather than self-reflection.
sentences.zh: 这段心路历程的一部分就与情绪性进食有关，它是通过进食来回应内心的感受，而不是通过自我反省。

sentences.en: And I think I've come to realize that in many ways it has damaged my ability to really listen to my body.
sentences.zh: 我想我逐渐意识到，在许多方面，这已经损害了我真正倾听自己身体的能力。

sentences.en: It's also brought a lot of shame that I think is still present.

sentences.en: Shame that I think doesn't really have a place when it comes to taking care of our bodies, taking care of our vessel, our home.
sentences.zh: 这种羞耻感，在我们需要照顾自己的身体、照顾我们这个躯壳和家园时，其实根本没有立足之地。

sentences.en: So what I really want this episode to be for you is a guide to unpacking the kind of psychological distinction between emotional and physical hunger.

sentences.en: And I want you to be able to see why your own relationship with food may have been impacted by things like diet culture,

sentences.en: is shamed for just choosing to eat what they like when emotional eating is actually so much more than responding to what your body craves and fulfilling that need.
sentences.zh: 我希望这一点能非常明确。

sentences.en: I want that to be really clear.
sentences.zh: 情绪性进食绝不仅仅是偶尔吃一些所谓的“不健康”食物或社会认为不好的食物的对立面。

sentences.en: Emotional eating isn't just the opposite of eating quote unquote unhealthy or eating foods that society may deem as bad every now and again.
sentences.zh: 情绪性进食不仅仅是饮食习惯不好。

sentences.en: Emotional eating is not just having a poor diet.
sentences.zh: 它发生在我们出于饥饿或生理需求之外的原因进食时。

sentences.en: It occurs when we eat for reasons other than hunger or physical necessity.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们把食物当作一种应对痛苦情绪、不舒服情绪的方式，或者将其作为对困扰我们的更深层问题的分心手段。

sentences.en: It's where we use food as a way to cope with difficult feelings, uncomfortable feelings, or as a distraction to some deeper problem that's bothering us.

sentences.en: It's subconscious.

sentences.zh: 吃什么

sentences.en: Something I always like to remind myself and you guys as well is that food does not have a moral label or a moral value.

sentences.en: It's literally an inanimate object.
sentences.zh: 它字面意思上就是一个无生命的物体。

sentences.en: It's just food.
sentences.zh: 它就只是食物。

sentences.en: It has no deeper attachment to who you are, to what your value is.
sentences.zh: 它与你是谁、你的价值是什么，并没有更深层的联系。

sentences.en: And yet we have been convinced that to eat some foods is to be hurting our body, is to not have self-discipline, is to not care about our well-being.
sentences.zh: 然而我们却被灌输了一种观念：吃某些食物就是在伤害我们的身体，就是缺乏自律，就是不关心自己的健康。

sentences.en: So of course, we have begun to treat it as a way to self-punish or to mediate our emotions.
sentences.zh: 所以理所当然地，我们开始把它当作一种自我惩罚或调节情绪的方式。

sentences.en: I think the easiest way we can identify when we're eating from a place of needing emotional
sentences.zh: 我想，我们要识别自己是因为需要情感上的

sentences.en: comfort or fulfillment is by noticing the difference between physical hunger and emotional hunger.
sentences.zh: 安慰或满足而去进食，最简单的方法就是注意生理性饥饿和情绪性饥饿之间的区别。

sentences.en: So physical hunger develops over time, whilst emotional hunger comes on really suddenly,
sentences.zh: 生理性饥饿是逐渐产生的，而情绪性饥饿则来得非常突然，

sentences.en: often in response to some kind of trigger that causes you to become stressed or overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 通常是对某种导致你感到压力或不知所措的诱因的反应。

sentences.en: So you're looking for something to kind of mediate those emotions, to make you feel better.
sentences.zh: 所以你会寻找某种东西来调节这些情绪，让你感觉好一点。

sentences.en: When we are physically hungry as well, we notice being full and we take it as a cue to stop
sentences.zh: 当我们感到生理性饥饿时，我们也会注意到自己饱了，并把它当作停止

sentences.en: eating, whereas when we're experiencing emotional hunger, we really don't feel completely full
sentences.zh: 进食的信号；而当我们经历情绪性饥饿时，我们其实并不会感到完全饱腹，

sentences.en: until after we've stopped, until the aftermath of whatever we've just eaten and we don't feel well, we feel sick, we wish that we had kind of stopped earlier, we don't feel like
sentences.zh: 直到我们停下来之后，直到我们刚吃完的东西产生后续反应，我们感觉不舒服、恶心，希望自己当时能早点停下来，我们不觉得自己

sentences.en: we've actually given our body the proper nutrients that maybe it deserves.
sentences.zh: 真的给身体提供了它可能应得的适当营养。

sentences.en: Physical hunger is often predictable.
sentences.zh: 生理性饥饿通常是可以预测的。

sentences.en: If we haven't eaten in the last four hours or so, maybe longer, we know that our body is
sentences.zh: 如果我们过去四个小时左右没吃东西，或者更久，我们就知道身体

sentences.en: going to start craving nutrients and energy, it's going to start grumbling, whereas emotional hunger is just going to happen whenever, wherever.
sentences.zh: 开始渴望营养和能量，开始咕咕叫了；而情绪性饥饿随时随地都会发生。

sentences.en: The reason for this is that food means more to our body than just nutrients and energy.
sentences.zh: 出现这种情况的原因是，食物对我们的身体而言不仅仅是营养和能量。

sentences.en: It's cultural, it's mental, it's social.
sentences.zh: 它是文化的，是精神的，是社交的。

sentences.en: We see that in how food is a massive part of how every single culture in the world celebrates or connects.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从食物是世界上每一个文化庆祝或建立联系的重要组成部分这一点中看到这一点。

sentences.en: We see that in how different foods make us feel a different way.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从不同的食物让我们有不同的感觉中看到这一点。

sentences.en: The fact that we have concepts such as comfort foods, the foods that elicit some kind of
sentences.zh: 我们有“慰藉食物”（comfort foods）这个概念，这些食物能引发某种

sentences.en: emotional reaction of either nostalgia or warmth or contentment, and then it comes down to things
sentences.zh: 怀旧、温暖或满足感的情绪反应，归根结底还在于

sentences.en: like taste and flavor and the impact of certain ingredients or contents, how they impact our brain, particularly through their influence on our hormones and our neurotransmitters.
sentences.zh: 诸如滋味、风味以及某些成分的影响，它们如何影响我们的大脑，特别是通过它们对我们的荷尔蒙和神经递质的影响。

sentences.en: Essentially, both of those things are the building blocks for our everyday emotional state.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，这两者都是我们日常情绪状态的基础。

sentences.en: So from a biological point, we all know that we need to eat to sustain our physical well-being,
sentences.zh: 因此，从生物学的角度来看，我们都知道我们需要进食来维持身体健康，

sentences.en: but currently, from all the recent studies conducted on this, we also know that it has a lot to do with pleasure.
sentences.zh: 但目前，根据对此进行的所有最新研究，我们也知道这与快乐息息相关。

sentences.en: All acts of eating increases dopamine in our brains, and it lights up our reward system.

sentences.en: But that is especially the case when we eat foods that are high in fat and sugar.
sentences.zh: 但当我们吃高脂肪和高糖的食物时，情况尤其如此。

sentences.en: Because if we think about this evolutionarily, those foods are often the highest in energy, such that they are more likely to provide us with those fat stores that previously were
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们从演化的角度来思考，这些食物通常能量最高，因此它们更有可能为我们提供那些以前

sentences.en: crucial for our survival.
sentences.zh: 对我们的生存至关重要的脂肪储备。

sentences.en: So our brains will create cues, internal cues, pleasure cues, to motivate us to consume these more by making us feel happier in association.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的大脑会创造信号，内部信号、快乐信号，通过让我们产生更快乐的联想，来激励我们消耗更多这些食物。

sentences.en: So food has this inherent impact on our brain through its impact on the dopamine system, which
sentences.zh: 因此，食物通过对多巴胺系统的影响，对我们的大脑产生这种内在影响，

sentences.en: is responsible for the release of things like dopamine, of course, but also serotonin and oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 多巴胺系统自然负责释放多巴胺等物质，当然也包括血清素和催产素。

sentences.en: And this is the biological basis for emotional eating.
sentences.zh: 这就是情绪性进食的生物学基础。

sentences.en: Consuming foods in order to improve our mood through that biological relationship, rather than for hunger or some physical advantage.
sentences.zh: 为了通过这种生物学关系改善情绪而摄入食物，而不是为了饥饿或某种生理优势。

sentences.en: For example, when we are feeling bored, we often gravitate towards food that offer a really rich flavor profile.
sentences.zh: 例如，当我们感到无聊时，我们往往会被提供非常浓郁风味的食物所吸引。

sentences.en: Or we'll eat more, not because of actual taste or that biological impact down the line, but because the act of eating in itself is a task that can keep our mind entertained.
sentences.zh: 或者我们会吃得更多，不是因为实际的味道或随之而来的生物学影响，而是因为进食这一行为本身就是一项可以让我们的思想保持专注的任务。

sentences.en: By chewing, by tasting, by putting things in our mouth, by swallowing, that is a physical activity.

sentences.en: So we want to build back up those energy stores.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想要重建这些能量储备。

sentences.en: And then when we're sad, when we're heartbroken, we often have a less of an appetite due to that distress and that deep hurt.
sentences.zh: 然后当我们伤心、心碎时，由于这种痛苦和深切的创伤，我们的食欲往往会下降。

sentences.en: So our bodies want to get the most energy from consuming as little food as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的身体希望通过摄入尽可能少的食物来获得最多的能量。

sentences.en: That means high fat, high energy, ice cream, chocolate, very much what we would call the heartbreak diet of Hollywood, what we see in movies.
sentences.zh: 这意味着高脂肪、高能量、冰淇淋、巧克力，非常符合我们所谓的荷里活“失恋减肥法”，我们在电影里看到的那种。

sentences.en: But it's probably also scientifically correct.
sentences.zh: 但这可能也是科学上正确的。

sentences.en: And after a period of intense heartbreak, that means that we are more inclined to go for those sugary snacks without really understanding our hunger.

sentences.en: A lot of these examples, as you may have gathered, have to do with attempts to rein in our stress response.

sentences.en: And that is because the act of eating certain food groups, certain foods, and our experiences of anxiety are causally related.
sentences.zh: 那是因为摄入某些食物类别、某些食物的行为与我们对焦虑的体验有着因果关系。

sentences.en: They're correlated in quite a multi-directional way.
sentences.zh: 它们以相当多维的方式相互关联。

sentences.en: So whilst we might search for some type of food we think is going to make us feel better in a time of heightened anxiety, it kind of has the counter effect.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然我们可能会寻找某种我们认为能在高度焦虑时让我们感觉好一点的食物，但它却有一种相反的效果。

sentences.en: It makes it worse.
sentences.zh: 它让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: But it's not just what that food provides, like we spoke about with emotional eating in response to boredom.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是食物所提供的东西，就像我们之前讨论的为了应对无聊而进行的情绪性进食一样。

sentences.en: Sometimes the physical act of consuming something or not consuming something, using food to provide
sentences.zh: 有时候，消耗某物或不消耗某物的生理行为，利用食物来提供

sentences.en: an emotional catharsis to symbolically act to fill your stomach and feel like you're fulfilling your emotional needs, that is so satisfying and it causes us to emotionally eat.
sentences.zh: 一种情感宣泄，象征性地填满你的胃，感觉你正在满足你的情感需求，这是非常令人满意的，它会导致我们情绪性进食。

sentences.en: And when we talk about the stress response, the experiences of fear, some studies have shown that when we eat, we provide a cue to our brain that we are safe.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论压力反应、恐惧体验时，一些研究表明，当我们进食时，我们是在向大脑发出我们是安全的信号。

sentences.en: You know, if we are actively in fight or flight mode, trying to escape some threat, we're not going to stop for a snack.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们正处于战斗或逃跑模式，试图逃避某种威胁，我们是不会停下来吃零食的。

sentences.en: Our appetite is suppressed when we feel danger.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到危险时，我们的食欲会被压抑。

sentences.en: And we are focused on overcoming whatever we are experiencing, whatever we are fearful of.
sentences.zh: 我们专注于克服我们正在经历的任何事情，我们所恐惧的任何事情。

sentences.en: But when we eat, when we force our bodies to consume something, to sit, to have a meal or a snack, our brain goes, OK, well, we can't be in immediate danger because otherwise we
sentences.zh: 但当我们进食时，当我们迫使身体消耗某些东西、坐下来、吃一顿饭或吃点零食时，我们的大脑就会想：好吧，我们不可能是处于直接危险之中，否则

sentences.zh: 我们现在就不会做这种事了。

sentences.en: We wouldn't be doing this.
sentences.zh: 我们不会做这个的。

sentences.en: So we must be OK.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一定没事。

sentences.en: It gives your brain a cue to calm down, to stop panicking.
sentences.zh: 它给你的大脑一个信号，让你冷静下来，停止恐慌。

sentences.en: So that is another way that stress is mediated by what we choose to eat when we choose to eat it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是通过我们选择吃什么以及何时选择吃来调节压力的另一种方式。

sentences.en: Not from a place of physical hunger, but an emotional need.
sentences.zh: 不是出于生理饥饿，而是出于情感需求。

sentences.en: You know, what I think that scientific explanation tells us, what I think is most crucial to take
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这些科学解释告诉我们的、我认为从中汲取的最关键的东西是，

sentences.en: from this is that we can't really blame ourselves for using food to self-medicate or regulate our emotions.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不能责怪自己利用食物来自我疗愈或调节情绪。

sentences.en: Nor can we just see it as an us problem, that we lack discipline, that we're weak.
sentences.zh: 我们也不能仅仅把它看作是我们自己的问题，认为我们缺乏纪律、我们很脆弱。

sentences.en: And therefore, I think what happens when we take on that perspective is that we self-inflict
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为当我们接受这种观点时，我们会在我们伤心、无聊、不知所措或压力大时所吃的食物周围

sentences.en: a lot of shame around the foods that we consume when we're sad or we're bored or we're overwhelmed or we're stressed.
sentences.zh: 产生大量的羞耻感。

sentences.en: Because the nature of this is that this habit comes from a lot of factors outside of our control.
sentences.zh: 因为这种习惯的本质来自于许多我们无法控制的因素。

sentences.en: Some of them are just innately biological, like our stress response.
sentences.zh: 其中一些纯粹是生物学上的，比如我们的压力反应。

sentences.en: Others are societal and cultural.
sentences.zh: 其他的则是社会的和文化的。

sentences.en: And a lot of them are to do with diet culture and how our health system approaches things like weight and things like calories and things like energy intake.

sentences.en: Our current approach to food, especially in a lot of Western societies, has become increasingly
sentences.zh: 我们目前对待食物的方法，特别是在许多西方社会，已经变得越来越

sentences.en: focused on restriction or focused on, you know, nutritional and energy intake, on BMI and what is and is not a healthy weight, as well as kind of, you know, alongside that, as we

sentences.en: But those diets are really all kind of telling us the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但这些减肥法其实都在告诉我们同一件事。

sentences.zh: 有一种正确进食的方式。

sentences.en: It tells us that what we choose to put in our bodies needs to be carefully controlled, whether
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们，我们选择放进身体里的东西需要被仔细控制，

sentences.zh: 无论是生酮饮食、间歇性断食还是生食饮食之类的，无论它是什么，甚至是果汁排毒。

sentences.en: And you know what that does?
sentences.zh: 你知道这会带来什么吗？

sentences.en: It puts us at war with food.
sentences.zh: 它让我们与食物开战。

sentences.en: It completely damages and disrupts our relationship and our perception of what food is as something
sentences.zh: 它彻底破坏并扰乱了我们对食物的关系和感知，将其视为需要被调节的东西，而不是燃料，而不是除了水、空气和食物之外的主要生命来源之一。

sentences.en: that needs to be regulated rather than as fuel, rather than as one of the main sources of life alongside, you know, it's water, air and food.
sentences.zh: 那些是我们真正需要的三样东西。

sentences.en: Those are the three things that we really need.
sentences.zh: 那些是我们真正需要的三样东西。

sentences.en: And I think it's really interesting because you never see someone controlling how much water they drink or trying to stop how much they breathe.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这很有趣，因为你从来没见过有人控制自己喝多少水，或者试图阻止自己呼吸多少次。

sentences.en: But we do have this intense feeling that food needs to be disciplined.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实有这种强烈的感觉，认为食物需要被管束。

sentences.en: Whereas these other sources of life, we don't have that feeling.
sentences.zh: 而对于这些其他的生命之源，我们却没有这种感觉。

sentences.en: We don't feel like there's a problem.
sentences.zh: 我们不觉得那是个问题。

sentences.en: When we feel made to put something on a pedestal like that, that is the easiest way to get something to control you.
sentences.zh: 当我们觉得某种东西被奉若神明时，那是让某物控制你的最简单的方法。

sentences.en: When we are taught to avoid something like certain foods, the more you want them because they feel more important.
sentences.zh: 当我们被教导要去避免某些食物时，你反而会更想要它们，因为它们感觉更重要。

sentences.en: They feel more elusive.
sentences.zh: 它们感觉更难以企及。

sentences.en: And so when we face something like intense emotions, a lot of stress and our impulse control is lessened because we're trying to navigate so much else, the first thing you're going

sentences.zh: 你将会反抗你一直施加给自己的这种限制。

sentences.en: You're not going to be aware of your appetite and you'll overeat.
sentences.zh: 你不会意识到自己的食欲，然后你会吃过量。

sentences.en: And then afterwards, you'll probably feel shame and you'll feel that shame, not because you deserve to feel shame, but because there is so much information coming from so many
sentences.zh: 然后在那之后，你可能会感到羞耻，你会感到羞耻，不是因为你活该感到羞耻，而是因为有太多的信息从太多的

sentences.en: sources telling you that if you binge eat, if you eat a certain food, that makes you
sentences.zh: 渠道告诉你，如果你暴饮暴食，如果你吃了某种食物，这就让你成为了一个不健康的人，

sentences.en: an unhealthy person, that makes you a bad person, that eating that food is bad and all your brain is actually trying to do in that moment is just emotionally regulate.
sentences.zh: 这就让你成为了一个坏人，吃那个食物是坏事，而你大脑在那一刻实际上试图做的只是调节情绪。

sentences.en: It's just trying to get you back to a safe mental place.
sentences.zh: 它只是想让你回到一个安全的心灵港湾。

sentences.en: I think part of understanding this is acknowledging that your environment is going to impact behaviors like diet based on what we've been convinced is normal or good for us.

sentences.en: And social media is part of that environment.
sentences.zh: 而社交媒体就是这种环境的一部分。

sentences.en: So we really need to de-influence ourselves a little bit when it comes to managing our emotional eating.
sentences.zh: 所以在管理情绪性进食方面，我们真的需要对自己的思想进行一下“反洗脑”。

sentences.en: And the best thing for you to do in that moment is to realize that what someone else is doing, what someone else is saying on TikTok,
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，你最好做的事情就是意识到别人在做什么，别人在TikTok上说什么，

sentences.zh: 你知道的，无论他们的“我一天吃什么”视频里有什么，

sentences.en: day video is probably not going to be right for you.
sentences.zh: 可能都不适合你。

sentences.en: There's always going to be some fad diet or craze or new way to fuel your body or lose weight.
sentences.zh: 总会有一些风靡一时的减肥法、热潮或为身体提供燃料或减重新途径。

sentences.en: And that leads us to form an unhealthy relationship with food, one that is not based on feeding
sentences.zh: 这导致我们与食物形成了一种不健康的关系，这种关系不是建立在用身体所需的东西来滋养身体的基础上，

sentences.en: our body with what it needs, but intertwined with things like our self-worth, our self-esteem, our sense of value.
sentences.zh: 而是与我们的自我价值、自尊、价值观交织在一起。

sentences.en: It's more based on our mood, particularly how we use food once again to make us feel better or make us feel worse, depending on how we're feeling in the moment.
sentences.zh: 它更多地基于我们的情绪，特别是我们如何再次利用食物来让我们感觉更好或更糟，这取决于我们此刻的感受。

sentences.en: That's why we emotionally eat.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们情绪性进食的原因。

sentences.en: We feel like eating is no longer this natural thing.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得进食不再是一件自然的事。

sentences.en: It's this has this bigger, deeper role, has this bigger, deeper meaning rather than just this normal, natural purpose to fuel our bodies.
sentences.zh: 它具有了更大、更深的角色，具有了更大、更深的意义，而不仅仅是为了给我们的身体提供能量这一正常、自然的目的。

sentences.en: I want to state again, I know I just spoke about it, but there really shouldn't be any shame around this if this is a behavior that you find yourself engaging in.
sentences.zh: 我想再次声明，我知道我刚刚才谈过，但如果你发现自己有这种行为，真的不应该对此感到任何羞耻。

sentences.en: Like I said, it's something that I've acknowledged I do quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，这是我已经承认自己经常做的事情。

sentences.en: And I used to think that meant I was weak or that I didn't care about my body, that I had, I should have had more control.
sentences.zh: 我过去常常认为这意味着我很软弱，或者我不关心自己的身体，认为我本该有更多的控制力。

sentences.en: And what I realized now is that that was really the influence of diet culture being the angry little kind of devil on my shoulder.
sentences.zh: 而我现在意识到，那其实是减肥文化的影响，就像我肩上那个愤怒的小恶魔。

sentences.en: You know, this tendency comes from so many things outside of our control, but they make us feel

sentences.en: like food controls us, makes us feel like what we're putting in our body is necessary for handling our emotions and that can have a lot of impacts.
sentences.zh: 让我们觉得我们放进身体里的东西是处理情绪所必需的，这会产生很多影响。

sentences.en: You know, emotional eating can have really distressing effects by leading to feelings of guilt, but it can also make us feel really ill or it can give us a big sugar crash a few
sentences.zh: 你知道，情绪性进食会导致内疚感，从而产生非常痛苦的效果，但它也会让我们感觉很不舒服，或者在几个小时后

sentences.zh: 情绪性进食的问题之一在于，它当然会影响你的身体感受，

sentences.zh: 特别是当我们吃得过多时，因为它会降低我们的能量水平，还会引起头痛。

sentences.en: It generally just causes some discomfort and we're not really resolving the problem.
sentences.zh: 它通常只是引起一些不适，而我们并没有真正解决问题。

sentences.en: So we're just kind of at a loss loss.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是有点不知所措、一无所获。

sentences.en: So how can we have that more intuitive relationship with the things we're putting in our body and notice the emotional triggers or causes of our dietary behaviors?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何才能与放进身体里的东西建立这种更直观的关系，并注意到我们饮食行为背后的情绪触发因素或原因呢？

sentences.zh: 让我们先把一件事搞清楚、弄明白。

sentences.en: Right now, sometimes you've had a rough day and that just really calls for some Uber Eats, some pizza, an iceburger, some ice cream.
sentences.zh: 当下，有时你度过了艰难的一天，这确实需要来点外卖、披萨、冰汉堡或者冰淇淋。

sentences.en: There is nothing wrong with that.

sentences.en: You don't need to feel guilt about wanting a certain food as long as it's not masking an underlying emotional need that you're not fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 你不必因为想吃某种食物而感到内疚，只要它不是在掩盖你未被满足的潜在情感需求。

sentences.en: But food can be really comforting and may be the exact thing that you need in that moment to energize yourself, to restore those levels.
sentences.zh: 但食物确实能带来极大的安慰，也可能正是你那一刻恢复精力、补充能量所急需的东西。

sentences.en: We also naturally experience cravings for certain foods that don't have an emotional basis, even if they are psychological.
sentences.zh: 我们也会自然而然地渴望某些并非出于情感基础的食物，即便它们具有心理层面的因素。

sentences.en: And I want to explain that a little bit further.
sentences.zh: 我想对此作进一步的解释。

sentences.en: So cravings are an intense, specific desire for a certain type of food.
sentences.zh: 所以，食欲是对某种特定食物的一种强烈、具体的渴望。

sentences.en: And it's in response to needing a certain kind of nourishment that our bodies are maybe not getting.
sentences.zh: 它是对我们身体可能没有得到的某种营养的需求作出的反应。

sentences.en: But they also come from our environment, like advertisements, which are deliberately created in a specific way to target you, to make you want something, to make you buy it.
sentences.zh: 但它们也源于我们的环境，比如广告，它们是经过精心设计的，旨在针对你，让你渴望某样东西，让你去买它。

sentences.en: So sometimes that can get confusing because we don't actually know what our body is needing.
sentences.zh: 所以有时这会让人感到困惑，因为我们实际上并不知道身体需要什么。

sentences.en: We are being cued by our environment.
sentences.zh: 我们在受环境的提示。

sentences.en: We do have those emotional needs.
sentences.zh: 我们确实有那些情感需求。

sentences.en: And sometimes our body just needs that nourishment.
sentences.zh: 有时我们的身体就是需要那种营养。

sentences.en: It's kind of impossible, right?
sentences.zh: 这有点不可能，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, on one side, the side of diet culture,
sentences.zh: 你知道，一方面，在饮食文化这一边，

sentences.en: we're being influenced to always make perfect decisions towards food as if there is actually a definition of perfect or that means anything.
sentences.zh: 我们受到影响，总是在食物上做出完美的决定，就好像“完美”真的有个定义，或者这有什么意义似的。

sentences.en: And then on the other side, this mass marketing side, they're trying to get you to buy that burger, to buy that chocolate bar.
sentences.zh: 而在另一方面，即大众营销这一边，他们正试图让你去买那个汉堡，买那块巧克力。

sentences.en: Those, you know, constant opposing narratives makes it so once again, food is no longer just food.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些不断冲突的说法，使得食物再次不仅仅是食物。

sentences.en: So how do we ignore all of that?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何忽视这一切呢？

sentences.en: How do we tap into what our bodies actually need?
sentences.zh: 我们如何去了解身体真正需要什么？

sentences.en: And what is the role of emotional eating in that equation?
sentences.zh: 情绪性进食在这个等式中又扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: Firstly, I don't think that demonizing certain foods or restrictive eating is going to help you at all, especially if what you're struggling with is emotional eating.
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为妖魔化某些食物或克制饮食对你毫无帮助，特别是当你正在与情绪性进食作斗争时。

sentences.en: It just doesn't work for most people because, A, it assumes that your behavior is due to a lack of self-control.
sentences.zh: 这对大多数人来说根本不管用，因为第一，它假定你的行为是因为缺乏自控力。

sentences.en: Therefore, it's something that you need to restrict, which just is not the case.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是你需要克制的事情，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: B, you're using food to fight an emotional problem.
sentences.zh: 第二，你在用食物来对抗情感问题。

sentences.en: And so it's the emotional problem that we need to work on, not the actual food consumption.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要解决的是情感问题，而不是实际的食物消费。

sentences.en: So restricting is only going to elevate that emotional stress because it's just one more thing to manage, one more thing to control.
sentences.zh: 因此，克制只会增加这种情绪压力，因为这又多了一件需要管理、需要控制的事情。

sentences.en: Eating may feel good in the moment.
sentences.zh: 进食在当下可能会感觉很好。

sentences.en: Restricting may feel like you're doing something, but the feelings that triggered you to emotionally eat are still going to be there.
sentences.zh: 克制可能会让你觉得你正在做点什么，但那些触发你情绪性进食的感觉依然会存在。

sentences.en: And finally, demonizing imposes shame.
sentences.zh: 最后，妖魔化会带来羞耻感。

sentences.en: When we think that we've slipped up, we get stuck in the shame cycle of, why did I do that?
sentences.zh: 当我们觉得自己失控时，就会陷入“我为什么会这样”、“我感到非常内疚”、“我毫无自控力”的羞耻循环中。

sentences.en: I feel so guilty.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常内疚。

sentences.en: I have no self-control.
sentences.zh: 我毫无自控力。

sentences.en: And rather than just realizing that there's a lot more going on there than just self-discipline, maybe you're lacking the deeper coping skills and you just don't have them yet.
sentences.zh: 与其意识到这里面除了自律之外还有很多其他因素——也许你缺乏更深层的应对技巧，而你只是还未掌握它们——

sentences.en: What you're really doing is just making yourself feel, once again, guilt.
sentences.zh: 你实际上在做的事情，只是让自己再次感到内疚。

sentences.en: You're making yourself feel guilty for something that perhaps you've only just started to recognize, something that comes from a lot of deeper factors that is going to take work.
sentences.zh: 你让你自己为一件你可能才刚刚开始认识到的事情感到内疚，一件源于许多更深层次、需要付出努力去解决的因素的事情。

sentences.en: And I think it's just identifying that you can cope in a way that's going to leave you feeling better in all facets and areas of your life,
sentences.zh: 我认为这只是要明确一点：你可以用一种能让你在生活的方方面面都感觉更好的方式来应对，

sentences.en: not just by reducing that current feeling, but feeling more capable of handling all of those future situations where you're going to be stressed, you're going to be sad,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是通过减轻当下的那种感觉，而是让自己更有能力应对未来所有那些你会感到压力、会感到悲伤、

sentences.en: you're going to be tired.
sentences.zh: 会感到疲惫的时刻。

sentences.en: And food doesn't have to be your only solution.
sentences.zh: 而且食物不一定是你唯一的解决办法。

sentences.en: So in terms of overcoming, navigating emotional eating, the first thing we really need to do is identify our emotional triggers.
sentences.zh: 所以在克服、应对情绪性进食方面，我们真正需要做的第一件事是识别我们的情绪触发点。

sentences.en: The biggest one is, without a doubt, stress.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，最大的一点就是压力。

sentences.en: When we experience chronic stress, as is so often in our 20s when we got a whole lot of things on our plate, financial stress, relationship stress, career stress,
sentences.zh: 当我们经历慢性压力时——就像我们在20多岁时经常遇到的那样，我们有太多事情要处理，经济压力、人际关系压力、职业压力，

sentences.en: all of that and more, your body produces high levels of the stress hormone known as cortisol.
sentences.zh: 所有这些以及更多——你的身体会产生高水平被称为皮质醇的压力荷尔蒙。

sentences.en: So cortisol triggers cravings for salty, sweet, fatty foods, foods that are going to give you that burst of energy and that burst of pleasure.
sentences.zh: 所以皮质醇会引发对咸、甜、高脂肪食物的渴望，这些食物能给你带来爆发性的能量和快乐。

sentences.en: The more stress, particularly uncontrolled stress you have in your life, the more likely you are to turn to food for emotional relief.
sentences.zh: 你生活中的压力越大，尤其是无法控制的压力越多，你就越有可能求助于食物来获得情感上的解脱。

sentences.en: So we need a better way to deal with that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要一个更好的方法来处理这个问题。

sentences.en: One that is more mental, one that is more cognitive based in our thoughts.
sentences.zh: 一种更偏向心理、更基于我们思想认知的方法。

sentences.en: The best way that I have found to manage this is by doing something called a brain dump,
sentences.zh: 我发现管理这一问题的最好方法是做一件叫做“大脑倾倒”的事，

sentences.en: which is the act of just writing everything down that's going on in my brain without judgment, without prejudice, putting those emotions out there.
sentences.zh: 这其实就是把脑海中正在发生的一切不带判断、不带偏见地全部写下来，把那些情绪释放出来。

sentences.en: You know, I always say a problem written down is a problem halved.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我常说，写下来的问题就等于解决了了一半。

sentences.en: And other ways to manage stress is to find an outlet for that excessive cortisol that is causing you to emotionally eat because cortisol is really just your body's hormonal response to danger.
sentences.zh: 管理压力的其他方法是为导致你情绪性进食的过量皮质醇寻找一个宣泄口，因为皮质醇实际上只是你的身体对危险做出的荷尔蒙反应。

sentences.en: It's released from our adrenal glands.
sentences.zh: 它由我们的肾上腺释放。

sentences.en: It's a steroid hormone.
sentences.zh: 它是一种类固醇荷尔蒙。

sentences.en: It gives you more energy to fight your stresses.
sentences.zh: 它为你提供更多能量来对抗压力。

sentences.en: It releases more energy for you.
sentences.zh: 它为你释放更多的能量。

sentences.en: So directing that into something that's going to use those those sources up,
sentences.zh: 所以把这些能量引导到能够消耗这些资源、

sentences.en: use that excess amount up that's going to make you physically exhausted or mobile is great in those situations.
sentences.zh: 消耗掉那些过量部分的事情上去，让你在体力上精疲力竭或活动起来，在那种情况下是非常棒的。

sentences.en: My recent favorite has been boxing.
sentences.zh: 我最近最喜欢的是拳击。

sentences.en: I cannot shut up about it.
sentences.zh: 我简直停不下来谈论它。

sentences.en: If you are a close friend of mine, I'm obsessed.
sentences.zh: 如果你是我的密友，我简直对此着迷。

sentences.en: I'm addicted.
sentences.zh: 我上瘾了。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's really nothing like punching a bag over and over again to give yourself an emotional release and to use up that excessive cortisol in your body.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，没有什么比一次又一次地击打沙袋更能让你释放情绪、并消耗体内过剩皮质醇的了。

sentences.en: But running, cycling, pick your poison.
sentences.zh: 但跑步、骑自行车，随你挑吧。

sentences.en: It's all good.
sentences.zh: 都很好。

sentences.en: But especially if it's aerobic exercise rather than anaerobic exercise, that kind of cardio that's going to get your heart rate up.
sentences.zh: 但特别是如果是有氧运动而不是无氧运动，那种能让你的心率飙升的有氧运动。

sentences.en: It's going to allow you to use more energy.
sentences.zh: 它能让你消耗更多能量。

sentences.en: And all of that energy is just energy that's not being placed on your mind, energy that is being released from your body in a positive way.
sentences.zh: 所有这些能量只是不再施加于你大脑的能量，是以一种积极的方式从你体内释放出来的能量。

sentences.en: Also, when you're you know that you're kind of entering into a stressful season or period of life, this may be hard.
sentences.zh: 另外，当你明知自己即将进入一个充满压力的时期或生活阶段时，这可能会很难。

sentences.en: This may not be something that you feel capable of doing, but I would definitely say reduce how much caffeine you're consuming.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是一件你觉得自己有能力做到的事，但我绝对会建议减少咖啡因的摄入量。

sentences.en: Caffeine not only impacts our appetite, but it also makes and heightens those levels of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 咖啡因不仅会影响我们的食欲，还会制造并加剧那些焦虑水平。

sentences.en: I actually no longer drink caffeine at all for that very reason.
sentences.zh: 其实我正是出于这个原因，已经完全不喝咖啡因了。

sentences.en: It just made me so much more stressed, even though it would increase my focus and concentration.
sentences.zh: 它只会让我感到压力大得多，尽管它确实能提高我的注意力和专注力。

sentences.en: You know, it also meant that I wasn't in control of my energy levels and I would plummet or I would be either too high or too low.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这也意味着我无法掌控自己的能量水平，我的状态会骤降，或者要么太高要么太低。

sentences.en: I'd need to eat food to kind of bring me back in the middle.
sentences.zh: 我需要吃东西来把我拉回到中间状态。

sentences.en: And nowadays I don't find myself as depleted at the end of the day, needing that sugar rush, that, you know, that fat rush, that carb rush to push me back up.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我发现自己在一天结束时不再那么精疲力竭，不需要那种糖分的刺激、脂肪的刺激、碳水化合物的刺激来把我重新振作起来。

sentences.en: I can kind of listen to my body better rather than trying to use something external to release or heighten or decrease my emotions.
sentences.zh: 我能更好地倾听自己的身体，而不是试图用外部的东西来释放、提高或降低我的情绪。

sentences.en: The next trigger I think most associated with emotional eating is boredom.
sentences.zh: 我认为与情绪性进食最相关的下一个触发因素是无聊。

sentences.en: You know, when you're having a little lazy day at home and you keep opening the fridge, closing it, opening the pantry, you're not really hungry, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你在家里度过慵懒的一天，不断地打开冰箱、关上，打开食品储藏室，你其实并不是饿了，对吧？

sentences.en: You're just wanting something to do.
sentences.zh: 你只是想找点事做。

sentences.en: That might seem innocuous, but that is emotional eating, eating in response to your emotional state, that being boredom.
sentences.zh: 这看起来可能无伤大雅，但这就是情绪性进食，即针对你的情绪状态——也就是无聊——而进食。

sentences.en: Food is a way to occupy your time and your mind.
sentences.zh: 食物是打发时间和心思的一种方式。

sentences.en: So instead of needing to find excitement in food, in taste, in flavor, look externally for something to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，不要在食物、味觉和风味中寻找刺激，而应该去外界寻找别的事做。

sentences.en: Go for a nice long walk.
sentences.zh: 去散个舒服的长步。

sentences.en: Call a friend you haven't spoken to in a while.
sentences.zh: 给好久没联系的朋友打个电话。

sentences.en: That is always so lovely.
sentences.zh: 那总是非常美好。

sentences.en: Do some life admin, whatever it may be.
sentences.zh: 处理一些生活琐事，无论是什么都行。

sentences.en: I think it's important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: And obviously, if you want a snack, go for it.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你想吃点零食，那就吃吧。

sentences.en: But what we want to break here is this cycle of disrupting our natural hunger for emotional hunger.
sentences.zh: 但我们在这里想要打破的是这种用情绪性饥饿干扰自然饥饿的循环。

sentences.en: And boredom can really interrupt that relationship and those cues that we receive from our body.
sentences.zh: 而无聊确实会打断这种关系以及我们从身体接收到的信号。

sentences.en: If you're exhausted, take a nice bath, put on some candles.
sentences.zh: 如果你筋疲力尽，就泡个舒服的澡，点上蜡烛。

sentences.en: If you're lonely, engage in some nostalgic TV shows or movies.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到孤独，就看一些怀旧的电视剧或电影。

sentences.en: You have no idea how comforting that is.
sentences.zh: 你无法想象这有多大抚慰作用。

sentences.en: And just realize that you do have the agency and the mental strength to regulate your own emotions in a way that feels healthy, in a way that feels good for you.
sentences.zh: 只要意识到你确实拥有自主权和心理力量，能够以一种健康、对你好的方式来调节自己的情绪。

sentences.en: Secondly, to identify those triggers, we need to be curious.
sentences.zh: 其次，为了识别这些触发因素，我们需要保持好奇心。

sentences.en: If I'm not eating for hunger, what am I feeling here?
sentences.zh: 如果我不是因为饥饿而进食，我在这里究竟感受到了什么？

sentences.en: And understanding the why.
sentences.zh: 并且去理解“为什么”。

sentences.en: Why am I feeling that?
sentences.zh: 为什么我会这种感觉？

sentences.en: And why do I feel compelled to eat when I might not necessarily want to in this moment?
sentences.zh: 为什么在此时此刻我可能并非真的想吃，却又觉得非吃不可？

sentences.en: So I would say time is really important here.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，时间在这里非常重要。

sentences.en: Pause when those cravings hit and ask yourself, could I put off eating for five or 10 minutes?
sentences.zh: 当食欲来袭时停顿一下，问问自己，我能把进食推迟五到十分钟吗？

sentences.en: Is it real hunger that I'm experiencing?
sentences.zh: 我体验到的是真正的饥饿吗？

sentences.en: Is this mental or physical?
sentences.zh: 这是心理上的还是生理上的？

sentences.en: And you make the decision from there.
sentences.zh: 然后从那里做出决定。

sentences.en: It's okay to appreciate the impact that food has on your mood because it's a scientific one that serves a purpose.
sentences.zh: 感激食物对你情绪的影响是可以的，因为这是一种服务于特定目的的科学现象。

sentences.en: And to hold off completely, like we said, starts a pretty severe cycle of restricting.
sentences.zh: 而正如我们所说，完全克制会引发相当严重的节食循环。

sentences.en: So savor, don't consume.
sentences.zh: 所以，去细品，而不是去吞咽。

sentences.en: When we emotionally eat, we tend to do so very quickly and sometimes without even tasting the food.
sentences.zh: 当我们情绪性进食时，我们往往进行得很快，有时甚至都没尝出食物的味道。

sentences.en: But by slowing down, A, we learn not to fear the feelings that make us want to emotionally eat and just enjoy food when we want it.
sentences.zh: 但通过放慢速度，第一，我们学会了不惧怕那些让我们想要情绪性进食的感觉，并且在想吃的时候好好享受食物。

sentences.en: Food is not something that is on a pedestal.
sentences.zh: 食物并不是什么被高高捧起的东西。

sentences.en: Food is not something that you're not allowed to have.
sentences.zh: 食物并不是什么你被禁止拥有的东西。

sentences.en: And B, it actually allows us to listen to physical hunger instead of emotional hunger.
sentences.zh: 第二，它实际上让我们能够倾听生理上的饥饿，而不是情绪上的饥饿。

sentences.en: Also,
sentences.zh: 另外，

sentences.en: eating a nutrient-dense quality diet has associations with minimizing our risk of some of those mental health effects and experiences that we are trying to regulate with food.
sentences.zh: 摄入营养密集的高质量饮食，有助于将我们试图用食物来调节的某些心理健康影响和体验的风险降到最低。

sentences.en: So there was a 2019 study that showed eating a greater variety of nutrients and vitamins is associated with a better mood, reduced risk of depression, and a lot of other benefits.
sentences.zh: 因此，2019年的一项研究表明，摄入更多样化的营养素和维生素与更好的情绪、降低抑郁风险以及许多其他好处息息相关。

sentences.en: Food is fuel.
sentences.zh: 食物是燃料。

sentences.en: Food is energy.
sentences.zh: 食物是能量。

sentences.en: Food is a resource.
sentences.zh: 食物是资源。

sentences.en: It's not something that A, needs to control you.
sentences.zh: 它不是那种第一，需要控制你的东西。

sentences.en: So B, needs to be restricted.
sentences.zh: 所以第二，它不需要被克制。

sentences.en: Or C, needs to play any other part in life.
sentences.zh: 或者第三，需要在生活中扮演任何其他角色。

sentences.en: There's also been a lot of buzz recently behind this idea of intuitive eating.
sentences.zh: 最近，关于“直觉饮食”这个概念也有很多的讨论。

sentences.en: And honestly, I wasn't sure whether to talk about this because at first glance, I was kind of like, is this just another fad diet?
sentences.zh: 老实说，我一开始不确定要不要谈这个，因为乍一看，我有点觉得，这不又是一种跟风的节食法吗？

sentences.en: You know, especially when Gwyneth Paltrow is a big proponent, I'm a little bit skeptical.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，特别是当格温妮丝·帕特洛成为其大肆推崇者时，我难免有点怀疑。

sentences.en: But I did my research and I do think it's really valuable to speak on because for some it is a solution.
sentences.zh: 但我做了研究，并且我确实认为谈论它非常有价值，因为对某些人来说，它确实是一个解决方案。

sentences.en: It treats food the way that I think a lot of us should be treating it.
sentences.zh: 它以我认为我们许多人应该对待的方式来看待食物。

sentences.en: And it does move us towards a better relationship with what we eat.
sentences.zh: 它确实让我们朝着与所吃食物建立更好的关系迈进。

sentences.en: So intuitive eating, the key principles of this is basically kind of the antithesis of restrictive consumption.
sentences.zh: 所以，直觉饮食的关键原则基本上算是克制饮食的对立面。

sentences.en: It's about rejecting the diet mentality, which we, A plus for that, big tick of approval.
sentences.zh: 它关乎拒绝节食心态，对此我们要给第一点赞，给予大大的认可。

sentences.en: Honoring your hunger.
sentences.zh: 顺应你的饥饿感。

sentences.en: Once again, important when we're trying to counter emotional eating.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，当我们试图对抗情绪性进食时，这很重要。

sentences.en: Feeling your fullness.
sentences.zh: 感受你的饱腹感。

sentences.en: respecting your body, treating it with kindness and compassion and not shame.
sentences.zh: 尊重你的身体，用善良和同理心而不是羞耻感去对待它。

sentences.en: It's really about eating according to the cues that your body is giving you and about what it needs and wants rather than according to your emotions,
sentences.zh: 这实际上是根据你的身体给你的信号、根据它的需要和渴望来进食，而不是根据你的情绪，

sentences.en: to some deeper perspective on what you should be eating.
sentences.zh: 或者是根据你“应该”吃什么的更深层的观点来进食。

sentences.en: If your body wants carbs, give it carbs.
sentences.zh: 如果你的身体想要碳水化合物，就给它碳水化合物。

sentences.en: If it wants a big old salad, give it salad.
sentences.zh: 如果它想要一大盆沙拉，就给它沙拉。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 去吃吧。

sentences.en: Have some sugar.
sentences.zh: 吃点糖吧。

sentences.en: Have some salt.
sentences.zh: 吃点盐吧。

sentences.en: All of those things we've been told to avoid for some misinformed reason have a place.
sentences.zh: 由于种种误解，我们一直被告知要避免的所有这些东西，其实都有它们存在的意义。

sentences.en: But it's about balance.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于平衡。

sentences.en: It's about, once again, being intuitive.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，再次回归直觉。

sentences.en: I think one of the major benefits, according to some studies published in the National Library of Medicine,
sentences.zh: 我认为根据国家医学图书馆发表的一些研究，其中一个主要好处是

sentences.en: is intuitive eating is just somewhat better for our psychological well-being.
sentences.zh: 直觉饮食对我们的心理健康有一定程度的益处。

sentences.en: Because we're eating in accordance to our biological urges and what is natural for us,
sentences.zh: 因为我们是根据我们的生理冲动和对我们自然的方式进食，

sentences.en: rather than according to something that a diet is trying to tell us to do or to kind of the rollercoaster of our emotions.
sentences.zh: 而不是根据某种节食试图告诉我们去做的事情，或者受情绪的过山车般起伏所支配。

sentences.en: People experience fewer amounts, fewer levels of food guilt or shame.
sentences.zh: 人们会体验到更少数量、更低程度的食物内疚或羞耻感。

sentences.en: They have improved body image, but to eat intuitively, you really need to relearn the distinction that we've been saying this whole time.
sentences.zh: 他们的身体形象得到了改善，但要做到直觉进食，你真的需要重新学习我们一直在说的区别。

sentences.en: Physical hunger and emotional hunger, you need to trust that feedback loop between your stomach and your brain because our bodies have an exceptional,
sentences.zh: 生理饥饿与情绪饥饿，你需要相信胃和大脑之间的反馈循环，因为我们的身体有一种非凡的、

sentences.en: finely tuned way of telling us what we need nutritionally, biologically, hunger wise, rather than just emotionally.
sentences.zh: 微调的方式来告诉我们在营养、生理和饥饿方面真正需要什么，而不仅仅是情绪上的需求。

sentences.en: And what's really happening, I'm going to say it one more time, when we emotionally eat, we no longer see food as fuel.
sentences.zh: 真正发生的事情是，我再重复一遍，当我们情绪化进食时，我们不再把食物视为燃料。

sentences.en: We see it as a way to regulate our emotions, to make us feel better, but only temporarily, only in the moment.
sentences.zh: 我们把它看作是一种调节情绪、让我们感觉更好的方式，但只是暂时的，只在当下一刻。

sentences.en: I want to finish off this episode by just restating a few key points here.
sentences.zh: 我想通过重申几个关键点来结束这一集。

sentences.en: Firstly, emotional eating does not make you a bad person.
sentences.zh: 首先，情绪化进食并不意味着你是一个坏人。

sentences.en: It does not make you faulty.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你有什么毛病。

sentences.en: And of course, it's subjective as to whether you think that's a problem for you.
sentences.zh: 当然，至于你是否认为这对你来说是个问题，这因人而异。

sentences.en: Sometimes what we think we are controlling is emotional eating when really it's just actually restriction and avoidance.
sentences.zh: 有时我们以为自己在控制情绪化进食，但实际上那只是限制和回避。

sentences.en: If you find your behavioral intentions towards food or about controlling your calories or your weight,
sentences.zh: 如果你发现你对食物的行为意图，或者关于控制卡路里或体重的意图，

sentences.en: that I think is more in response to diet culture than I think emotional eating.
sentences.zh: 我认为这更多是对饮食文化的反应，而不是情绪化进食。

sentences.en: I think that emotional eating is only part of the problem there because you have been restricting yourself too much, avoiding it too much,
sentences.zh: 我认为情绪化进食只是其中的一部分问题，因为你对自己限制太多、回避太多，

sentences.en: that food has now been put on this pedestal such that when your emotions are heightened, you are more inclined to go for them because you have less impulse control.
sentences.zh: 以至于食物现在被捧得高高在上，当你的情绪高涨时，由于冲动控制力下降，你更倾向于去吃它们。

sentences.en: Secondly, this is obviously just my advice and my perspective on this and my research.
sentences.zh: 其次，这显然只是我的建议、我对这件事的看法以及我的研究。

sentences.en: There are different perspectives and different opinions.
sentences.zh: 有不同的观点和意见。

sentences.en: And you have agency when it comes to decisions you want to make towards your diet and how you process your emotions.
sentences.zh: 在决定你对饮食以及如何处理情绪的意愿时，你拥有自主权。

sentences.en: But I do think that we can benefit from feeling like we are in control of our behaviors, whether that has to do with eating or exercise or spending or self-destructive behaviors,
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，如果我们觉得自己能够控制自己的行为，无论是与饮食、运动、消费还是自毁行为有关，

sentences.en: whatever it may be, you are in control of them.
sentences.zh: 无论是什么，你都能掌控它们，我们都会从中受益。

sentences.en: We do not want food to feel like it controls us and like we have no power to stop or to start.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望食物让我们觉得它在控制我们，让我们觉得自己无力停止或开始。

sentences.en: And thirdly, I just sincerely hope that you enjoyed this episode and that you feel informed.
sentences.zh: 第三，我真诚地希望你喜欢这一集，并且觉得有所收获。

sentences.en: I think these things are rarely spoken about in a modern day culture that is obsessed with things like diets and fads and right or wrong and weight loss and calories.
sentences.zh: 我认为在现代文化中，这种事情很少被提及，现代文化痴迷于节食、潮流、对与错、减肥和卡路里。

sentences.en: Our relationship with food is so much more psychological than we think.
sentences.zh: 我们与食物的关系比我们想象的要心理化得多。

sentences.en: And I hope that that comes across and that you're able to look at your own eating habits and see when you're responding to emotional hunger instead of physical hunger.
sentences.zh: 我希望这个观点能传达给你，让你能够审视自己的饮食习惯，看出自己何时是在对情绪饥饿做出反应，而不是生理饥饿。

sentences.en: And if you want to make a choice around that, have the agency, have the information to be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你想围绕这一点做出选择，拥有自主权，拥有能够做到这一点的信息。

sentences.en: So thank you so much for listening to today's episode.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家收听今天的节目。

sentences.en: I really do hope that you enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我真心希望你们喜欢它。

sentences.en: This is something I'm learning with you.
sentences.zh: 这也是我和你们一起在学习的东西。

sentences.en: I find that talking about this is so interesting when I talk about it with friends and family and you really do examine how mental your dietary habits are.
sentences.zh: 我发现谈论这个非常有趣，当我与朋友和家人谈论它时，你真的会审视自己的饮食习惯有多么依赖心理。

sentences.en: It's something that I think I've been learning the better my relationship with food has become.
sentences.zh: 随着我和食物的关系变得越来越好，这也是我一直在学习的东西。

sentences.en: So I hope that you got something out of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你从中有所收获。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢它。
